papers.title: Clinical Risk Factors for Suicide in Persons With Epilepsy: A Nationwide Population-Based Case-Control Study.
papers.title_zh: 癫痫患者的自杀临床风险因素：一项基于全国人口的病例对照研究。
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Individuals with epilepsy face an elevated risk of suicide, but risk factors for suicide remain incompletely understood. We conducted a nationwide case-control study in Sweden to investigate clinical characteristics associated with suicide risk in persons with epilepsy.
METHODS: Persons with epilepsy were identified through Swedish nationwide registers, with epilepsy diagnoses validated through medical record review. Cases were individuals who died by suicide between 2006 and 2011, validated through autopsy reports, and controls were derived from the source population using similar validation procedures. Characteristics included epilepsy type, etiology, tonic-clonic seizure (TCS) frequency, antiseizure medication (ASM) treatment, living conditions, and psychiatric comorbidity. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% CIs were estimated using conditional logistic regression.
RESULTS: The study included 111 suicide cases and 1,147 controls. Suicide cases had a mean age at epilepsy onset of 20 years, and 35% were female. Alcohol abuse (OR 11.81, 95% CI 6.25-22.30) and other substance abuse (OR 10.71, 95% CI 4.52-25.38) showed stronger associations than depression (OR 2.94, 95% CI 1.56-5.53) and anxiety disorders (OR 2.93, 95% CI 1.57-5.44). Living alone was associated with increased risk (OR 2.59, 95% CI 1.58-4.26). Recent TCS showed a dose-response relationship, with the highest risk among individuals experiencing 4-10 TCS in the preceding year (OR 5.01, 95% CI 2.2-11.3). Structural and unknown epilepsy etiologies were associated with elevated risk (OR 3.07, 95% CI 1.0-9.5 and OR 8.80, 95% CI 2.9-27.1, respectively). ASM treatment was associated with lower suicide risk (monotherapy OR 0.51, 95% CI 0.27-0.95; polytherapy OR 0.21, 95% CI 0.1-0.5), and nonadherence was associated with higher risk (OR 3.02, 95% CI 1.8-5.1).
DISCUSSION: This study identified a distinct risk profile for suicide in persons with epilepsy, highlighting alcohol and substance abuse, living alone, seizure burden, nonadherence, and structural or unknown etiologies as key risk factors. The stronger associations for substance abuse may reflect characteristics specific to epilepsy populations and the focus on completed suicide. Screening for substance abuse and improved seizure control may contribute to suicide prevention. Major limitations include the modest number of cases and incomplete information on prior suicidal behavior.
papers.abstract_zh:
背景和目的：癫痫患者面临较高的自杀风险，但对自杀的风险因素仍未完全了解。我们在瑞典开展了一项全国性病例对照研究，以调查与癫痫患者自杀风险相关的临床特征。
方法：通过瑞典全国登记册识别癫痫患者，并通过病历审查对癫痫诊断进行验证。
病例为2006年至2011年间死于自杀的个体，通过尸检报告进行验证；对照组则使用类似的验证程序从源人群体中选出。特征包括癫痫类型、病因、强直-阵挛性发作（TCS）频率、抗癫痫药物（ASM）治疗、生活条件和精神疾病合并症。使用条件Logistic回归估算了95%置信区间（CI）的优势比（OR）。
结果：该研究包括111例自杀病例和1147例对照。自杀病例的癫痫发病平均年龄为20岁，其中35%为女性。酗酒（OR 11.81，95% CI 6.25-22.30）和其他药物滥用（OR 10.71，95% CI 4.52-25.38）与抑郁症（OR 2.94，95% CI 1.56-5.53）和焦虑症（OR 2.93，95% CI 1.57-5.44）相比，相关性更强。独居与风险增加相关（OR 2.59，95% CI 1.58-4.26）。
TCS 显示出剂量-反应关系，前一年经历 4-10 次 TCS 的个体风险最高（OR 5.01，95% CI 2.2-11.3）。结构性癫痫和病因不明的癫痫与风险升高相关（OR 3.07，95% CI 1.0-9.5和OR 8.80，95% CI 2.9-27.1）。ASM治疗与较低的自杀风险相关（单药治疗OR 0.51，95% CI 0.27-0.95；多药联合治疗OR 0.21，95% CI 0.1-0.5），并且不依从
NCE与较高风险相关（OR 3.02，95% CI 1.8-5.1）。
讨论：本研究确定了癫痫患者自杀的独特风险特征，强调酒精和药物滥用、独居、癫痫发作负担、不依从性以及结构性或未知病因是主要风险因素。药物滥用相关性更强，这可能反映了癫痫人群的特有特征，以及对已完成自杀的关注。
筛查药物滥用和改善癫痫发作控制可能有助于预防自杀。主要局限性包括病例数量较少以及既往自杀行为的信息不完整。

papers.title: The sodium channel SCN2A regulates cortical excitatory and inhibitory neurogenesis.
papers.title_zh: 钠离子通道SCN2A调节皮质兴奋性和抑制性神经发生。
papers.abstract: Voltage-gated sodium channels regulate neuronal excitability and synaptic transmission in the postnatal and adult brain. The gene SCN2A, encoding the sodium channel Nav1.2, regulates synaptic development and variants in SCN2A are associated with autism spectrum disorders (ASD) and a broad spectrum of epilepsy phenotypes, including early-onset developmental and epileptic encephalopathies. The expression pattern of SCN2A begins during prenatal cortical development, prior to the onset of synaptic transmission, but it is unknown whether SCN2A regulates early cortical development through mechanisms independent of synaptic transmission. Here we reveal that isogenic and ASD patient-derived human forebrain organoids modelling a loss of SCN2A function display impaired excitatory and inhibitory neurogenesis, leading to a developmental imbalance. Unexpectedly, we find precocious generation of cortical inhibitory neurons is driven by elevated Sonic hedgehog signaling and is reversible through pharmacological inhibition. Functionally, these developmental phenotypes arise due to Nav1.2-dependent sodium channel dysfunction and reduced action potential generation, leading to abnormal neuronal network activity. Our results identify a mechanism for cortical excitatory and inhibitory neurogenesis involving SCN2A, and reveal that early neurogenesis deficits precede postnatal neural circuit dysfunction in SCN2A-associated disorders.
papers.abstract_zh:
电压门控钠通道调节出生后和成年大脑中的神经元兴奋性和突触传递。编码钠通道Nav1.2的基因SCN2A调节突触发育，而SCN2A的变异与自闭症谱系障碍（ASD）和广泛的癫痫表型相关，包括早发性发育性和癫痫性脑病。SCN2A的表达模式始于产前皮质
在突触传递开始之前，SCN2A在皮层发育中起着关键作用，但目前尚不清楚SCN2A是否通过独立于突触传递的机制来调节早期皮层发育。本文揭示，模拟SCN2A功能丧失的同基因和ASD患者来源的人类前脑类器官表现出兴奋性和抑制性神经发生受损，导致发育失衡。出乎意料的是，我们发现皮质神经元过早生成，
抑制性神经元是由升高的Sonic hedgehog信号驱动的，并且可以通过药物抑制来逆转。在功能上，这些发育表型是由于Nav1.2依赖性钠通道功能障碍和动作电位产生减少而出现的，从而导致神经元网络活动异常。我们的结果确定了涉及SCN2A的皮层兴奋性和抑制性神经发生的机制，并揭示了早期神经发生
在SCN2A相关性疾病中，缺陷先于产后神经环路功能障碍发生。

papers.title: Pearls & Oy-sters: Anti-GABAA Receptor Encephalitis Presenting as Fulminant Hemicerebellitis in a 5-Year-Old Girl.
papers.title_zh: 珍珠和Oy-sters ：抗GABAA受体脑炎呈现为5岁女孩的爆发性半小脑炎。
papers.abstract: A previously healthy 5-year-old girl presented with several days of fever/malaise followed by acute neurologic decline. Head CT demonstrated fulminant right cerebellitis with edema and fourth-ventricle effacement concerning for impending herniation. She underwent emergent posterior fossa decompression. CSF showed mild pleocytosis, and MRI revealed right cerebellar nonenhancing T2/fluid-attenuated inversion recovery hyperintense lesions with evolving supratentorial cortical involvement. Despite empiric antimicrobials and initial immunotherapy (high-dose IV methylprednisolone and tocilizumab followed by IV immunoglobulin/plasma exchange), she developed progressive neuroinflammation with new seizures and markedly elevated CSF IL-6, prompting escalation to additional IL-6-directed therapy with tocilizumab and rescue intrathecal dexamethasone. She subsequently stabilized with radiographic improvement and meaningful neurologic recovery. Expanded antibody testing later confirmed anti-GABAA receptor (anti-GABAAR) encephalitis. This case highlights fulminant cerebellitis as a life-threatening presentation of anti-GABAAR encephalitis and underscores the importance of early posterior fossa decompression, parallel diagnostic evaluation (including expanded antibody panels), and coordinated, time-sensitive immunotherapy escalation in select critically ill presentations.
papers.abstract_zh:
一名此前健康的5岁女孩出现数日发热/不适，随后出现急性神经功能衰退。头部CT显示暴发性右侧小脑炎，伴有水肿和第四脑室受压，提示即将发生疝。她接受了紧急后颅窝减压术。脑脊液显示轻度细胞增多，MRI显示右侧小脑T2/液体衰减反转恢复序列高信号病灶，无强化，并有进展。
提示幕上皮质受累。尽管接受了经验性抗生素和初始免疫治疗（大剂量静脉注射甲泼尼龙和托珠单抗，随后静脉注射免疫球蛋白/血浆置换），但患者仍出现进行性神经炎症，伴有新的癫痫发作和脑脊液IL-6显著升高，因此加用托珠单抗和鞘内地塞米松作为补救措施，以进一步针对IL-6进行治疗。随后，她的病情稳定下来，影像学检查显示
改善和有意义的神经功能恢复。随后进行的扩展抗体检测证实了抗GABAA受体（抗GABAAR）脑炎。该病例突出了暴发性小脑炎作为抗GABAAR脑炎的一种危及生命的表现，并强调了早期后颅窝减压、并行诊断评估（包括扩大的抗体谱）以及在特定情况下协调、及时地强化免疫治疗的重要性。

papers.title: Azetukalner in Adults With Focal Seizures: The X-TOLE2 Phase 3 Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.title_zh: Azetukalner在局灶性癫痫发作成人中的应用： X-TOLE2 3期随机临床试验。
papers.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Despite more than 30 approved antiseizure medications, many individuals with focal epilepsy continue to experience seizures, indicating a persistent need for novel therapies.
OBJECTIVE: To determine efficacy and safety of the novel, potent KV7 channel opener azetukalner for treatment of focal seizures.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This phase 3, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial of azetukalner was conducted over a 12-week double-blind period (November 18, 2022, to February 3, 2026) at 138 sites in North America, South America, Europe, and Asia Pacific. Adults with focal epilepsy experiencing 4 or more focal seizures per month despite stable treatment with 1 to 3 antiseizure medications were enrolled. Data were analyzed using a dataset derived from the database lock dated February 26, 2026.
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomized 1:1:1 to receive placebo or 15 or 25 mg of azetukalner once daily with the evening meal for 12 weeks with no titration period. Participants completing the double-blind period could enter an open-label extension.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary efficacy end point was median percentage change from baseline in monthly (28-day) focal seizure frequency during the double-blind period for azetukalner vs placebo. Safety and tolerability were assessed by recording treatment-emergent adverse events, changes in clinical laboratory findings, vital signs, and electrocardiogram.
RESULTS: Of 607 adults screened, 374 participants (190 [50.8%] female; mean [SD] age, 40.0 [12.9] years) were enrolled, randomized and treated with placebo (125 participants), 15-mg azetukalner (125 participants), or 25-mg azetukalner (124 participants). Participants had a baseline median (IQR) of 12.75 (7.56 to 32.97) seizures per month and had previously tried and stopped a median (IQR) of 5 (3 to 8) antiseizure medications. Most (336 participants [89.8%]) were receiving 2 to 3 concomitant antiseizure medications. The median (IQR) change from baseline in monthly seizure frequency was -10.4% (-39.1% to 8.3%) for the placebo group, -34.5% (-61.6% to -12.3%) for the 15-mg azetukalner group (P < .001 vs placebo), and -53.2% (-77.2% to -28.8%) for the 25-mg azetukalner group (P < .001 vs placebo). Azetukalner was generally well tolerated, and treatment-emergent adverse events were comparable to those observed in the phase 2b X-TOLE trial.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This randomized clinical trial found that azetukalner demonstrated robust, rapid, and durable reductions in seizure frequency with a favorable benefit-risk profile. Treatment with azetukalner resulted in one of the largest median percentage reductions in seizure frequency vs placebo reported to date in patients with drug-resistant epilepsy, supporting azetukalner as a promising novel antiseizure medication with significant opportunity to improve clinical outcomes.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05614063.

papers.title: Optimizing antiseizure treatment in women of reproductive age and during pregnancy: Nationwide practice versus specialized epilepsy care in Poland.
papers.title_zh: 在育龄期妇女和妊娠期妇女中优化抗癫痫治疗：波兰的全国性实践与癫痫专科护理。
papers.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare antiseizure medication (ASM) treatment patterns among women with epilepsy (WWE) of reproductive age and pregnant WWE using nationwide administrative data and a university epilepsy referral center cohort in Poland.
METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed two complementary datasets. Nationwide data were obtained from the Polish National Health Fund, including 44,951 WWE aged 20-49 years in 2024 and 594 pregnant WWE who delivered in 2022. Referral center data were collected from medical records of 277 WWE aged 20-49 years treated in 2024 and 112 pregnancies managed between 2019 and 2026.
RESULTS: Levetiracetam and lamotrigine were the most frequently prescribed ASMs in both cohorts. Compared with the nationwide population, women of reproductive age treated at the epilepsy center were significantly less likely to receive valproate (18.4 % vs. 31.1 %, p < 0.001) or carbamazepine (6.5 % vs 16 %p < 0.001), while lacosamide, brivaracetam, and cenobamate were prescribed more frequently. The proportion of women receiving monotherapy was similar in both cohorts. Among pregnant WWE, non-valproate monotherapy predominated in both groups but was significantly more common at the referral center (77.7 % vs. 62.0 %, p < 0.001). Valproate use during pregnancy was markedly lower in the referral center than in the nationwide cohort (2.7 % vs. 16.0 %, p < 0.001), whereas levetiracetam and lamotrigine use was comparable.
CONCLUSIONS: Women managed at an epilepsy referral center were substantially less likely to receive potentially teratogenic ASMs, particularly valproate, despite representing a more clinically complex population. These findings highlight the contribution of specialized epilepsy care to optimizing pharmacological management for women of reproductive age and during pregnancy while supporting adherence to contemporary treatment recommendations.

papers.title: Seizure and psychiatric outcomes following epilepsy surgery in patients with preoperative interictal psychosis: A systematic review.
papers.title_zh: 术前发作间期精神病患者癫痫手术后的癫痫发作和精神病学结局：系统综述。
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interictal psychosis (IIP) is a severe psychiatric comorbidity of epilepsy, but its implications for epilepsy surgery and postoperative outcomes remain uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate seizure and psychiatric outcomes following resective epilepsy surgery in patients with preoperative IIP.
METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines and prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261362874). Observational studies reporting seizure and/or psychiatric outcomes in patients with preoperative IIP undergoing resective epilepsy surgery were included. The primary outcome was seizure freedom (Engel class I or equivalent), and the secondary outcome was sustained postoperative worsening of preexisting IIP.
RESULTS: Seven independent studies met the inclusion criteria. Among 59 patients with available seizure-outcome data, 38 achieved seizure freedom at last follow-up. Two comparative cohorts reported no statistically significant association between preoperative IIP and seizure freedom. In the only study using structured positive- and negative-symptom rating scales, 4 of 12 patients experienced sustained worsening of psychotic symptoms. Diagnostic definitions and psychiatric outcome assessments varied substantially across studies.
CONCLUSIONS: Available evidence is insufficient to determine whether preoperative interictal psychosis independently influences seizure or psychiatric outcomes following epilepsy surgery. Small samples, heterogeneous diagnostic definitions, inconsistent psychiatric assessments, and limited comparator data preclude firm conclusions. Future studies should use standardized operational definitions and longitudinal psychiatric assessments.

papers.title: Clinical value of video monitoring in seizure classification and medication decision-making: A questionnaire-based study in outpatients with epilepsy.
papers.title_zh: 视频监测在癫痫发作分类和用药决策中的临床价值：一项针对癫痫门诊患者的问卷调查研究。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical value of ictal video monitoring in refining seizure classification and guiding antiseizure medication (ASM) decisions in outpatients with epilepsy, and to examine the concordance between eyewitness descriptions and objective video evidence.
METHODS: In this questionnaire-based, single-center study, 525 patients with epilepsy who attended the neurology outpatient clinic of West China Hospital, Sichuan University, between July and September 2025 were enrolled. A self-designed questionnaire was used to collect demographic information, medication history, seizure types, eyewitness descriptions, ictal video recordings, and diagnostic classifications before and after video review. Patients with ictal videos were grouped by recording modality: mobile phone recording, surveillance footage, and video-EEG (VEEG) monitoring. Initial classification was performed without video; a second classification was then performed with video when available. Classifications were independently reviewed once by an experienced epilepsy-specialist neurologist, with final adjudication by a senior physician in cases of disagreement.Categorical variables were compared using the χ2 test or Fisher's exact test when expected frequencies were < 5, with two-sided P < 0.05 considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Ictal video recordings were available for 159 of 525 patients (30.3 %). Among the 159 patients with complete pre- and post-video diagnostic records, diagnostic revision occurred in 32 patients (20.1 %). The most common revision pathway was bilateral tonic-clonic seizure of unknown onset (BTC) to focal-to-bilateral tonic-clonic seizure (FBTC), accounting for 46.9 % (15/32) of all revisions. A determinate final seizure classification (focal or generalized) was more frequent in patients with ictal videos than in those without (96/159 [60.4 %] vs 121/366 [33.1 %], P < 0.001). ASM regimens were changed based on video evidence in 19/159 patients (11.9 %), and 16 patients required subsequent readjustment. Diagnostic revision rates were 15.2 % (19/125) for mobile phone recordings, 36.8 % (7/19) for surveillance footage, and 40.0 % (6/15) for VEEG monitoring. Diagnostic revision was significantly associated with ASM regimen changes (χ2 = 4.22, P = 0.040). An eyewitness was present at consultation for 512/525 patients (97.5 %), and the diagnostic concordance rate between eyewitness descriptions and video evidence was 89.9 %.
CONCLUSION: Ictal video recording was associated with clinically meaningful revision of seizure classification and influenced ASM decisions in outpatients with epilepsy, with higher diagnostic yield observed for more professional recording modalities. Video evidence may help correct classification bias arising from reliance on verbal history, particularly in identifying focal onset.

papers.title: Epilepsy Online Social Support: Characterizing topics and challenges shared in the r/Epilepsy community.

papers.abstract: Epilepsy is one of the most common neurological conditions, and people living with epilepsy (PLWE) often use social media as a resource. However, a comprehensive understanding of the topics represented in epilepsy-specific communities where PLWE may be more honest is essential to designing better technologies to address epilepsy self-management. To understand the main topics and concerns of PLWE, we collected 23,945 r/Epilepsy subreddit posts and performed topic modeling, thematic analysis, and psycholinguistic analysis. We found five major themes among those topics: symptoms and triggers (e.g., mental health and memory, sleep/nocturnal, and photosensitivity), treatment and healthcare experience (e.g., medication, understanding epilepsy), daily functions (e.g., perceived level of independence and finances), seizure activity (e.g., auras and ictal symptoms), and support for PLWE (assisting PLWE and support for PLWE). We highlight the top psycho-linguistic characteristics of posts across different topics. Our contributions include providing an understanding of the challenges of an online epilepsy community and their social support needs, and implications for designing technologies.

papers.title: Side-to-side and other complex head movements as ictal signs in epilepsy: A video-EEG case series and review of literature.
papers.title_zh: 作为癫痫发作体征的左右头部运动和其他复杂头部运动：视频-脑电图病例系列和文献回顾。
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.abstract: Side-to-side head shaking is often considered a distinctive clinical sign that differentiates functional seizures from epileptic seizures; however, it may also occur as an ictal phenomenon in focal epilepsy. We retrospectively reviewed all video-telemetry reports of patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy undergoing presurgical evaluation between 2015 and 2025. All reports were electronically screened for mentioning side-to-side or other complex head movements and the video-EEG of these patients was reviewed and included if associated with ictal EEG changes. Seventeen patients were identified who experienced 631 seizures in total, 201 of which included such movements (median: 2 per patient, range: 1-160). One patient (No. 5) accounted for 79% of these events and represented an outlier. Head movements were predominantly horizontal (93.5%), followed by mixed (5%) and rotatory (1.5%). While small-amplitude movements predominated overall, larger amplitudes were more frequent after excluding the outlier case. In six patients, head movements were the initial observed feature of seizure semiology and typically represented a brief component of the seizure, although prolonged in the outlier case. Interrater agreement ranged from fair to good across semiological variables. Presumed epileptogenic zones were heterogenous, including frontal, temporal, anterior quadrant, and hemispheric regions. Ictal side-to-side and other complex head movements can occur in focal epilepsies but lack localizing or lateralizing value. They likely reflect seizure propagation and involvement of broader neuronal circuits. Further studies are needed to clarify their mechanisms and clinical significance.

papers.title: Chemogenetic activation of parvalbumin interneurons in the piriform cortex alleviates hippocampal focal seizures.
papers.title_zh: 梨状皮质中小叶白蛋白中间神经元的化学发生激活可缓解海马局灶性癫痫发作。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The anterior piriform cortex (APC) is a limbic area closely associated with temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) but is understudied. Our previous study demonstrated that in the APC, parvalbumin-expressing (PV+) interneurons provide strong inhibition and help maintain excitation-inhibition balance. Here, we examined whether and how APCPV neurons can ameliorate seizure symptoms in TLE.
METHODS: We used a chronic intrahippocampal kainic acid (IHKA) mouse model that develops hippocampal pathology and spontaneous recurrent seizures (SRSs). APCPV neurons were chemogenetically activated, and local field potentials were recorded longitudinally from multiple regions. Seizure metrics, spectral power, and functional connectivity were compared between APCPV-activated and control samples.
RESULTS: Loss of PV+ synapses emerged in the APC during epileptogenesis. Selective activation of APCPV neurons reduced the frequency and duration of hippocampal SRSs and modified long-range dynamics, with region- and frequency-specific changes in interictal band power and functional connectivity.
SIGNIFICANCE: APCPV chemogenetic activation exerts a robust anti-seizure effect and identifies the APC as a promising cortical node for seizure network control. The associated spectral and connectivity signatures suggest that targeted modulation of APC microcircuits can rebalance distributed seizure networks and lower seizure recurrence.

papers.title: Patient characteristics and treatment patterns in Dravet syndrome and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome: real-world evidence from physician- and caregiver-reported data in Japan.
papers.title_zh: Dravet综合征和Lennox-Gastaut综合征的患者特征和治疗模式：来自日本医生和护理人员报告的数据的现实证据。
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dravet syndrome (DS) and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (LGS) are rare, severe childhood-onset developmental and epileptic encephalopathies associated with treatment-resistant seizures and significant cognitive, behavioral, and motor impairments, all of which require extensive support from caregivers.
OBJECTIVES: To describe real-world patient characteristics and treatment patterns in those with DS or LGS, and assess caregiver burden in Japan.
METHODS: Data for patients in Japan were analyzed descriptively from the Adelphi DS and LGS Disease Specific Programme™, a cross-sectional linked survey of physicians, patients, and caregivers (November 2022-August 2023).
RESULTS: Thirty-four physicians provided data for 81 patients (DS = 31; LGS = 50). Within the 4 weeks prior to data collection, the most common seizure types reported for patients with DS were generalized tonic-clonic (35%) and tonic (32%), and for patients with LGS were tonic (68%) and atypical absence (22%). In both DS and LGS, cognitive and language impairments were reported to be prevalent, and valproate and carbamazepine were reported to be the most common first-line treatments before and after diagnosis. Current treatment satisfaction among responding physicians was reported to be moderate (somewhat satisfied: DS 56%; LGS 45%). Caregivers (n = 25) reported that managing seizures was the most difficult aspect of care for patients with DS or LGS. Moreover, many reported an impact of caregiving on their own health.
CONCLUSIONS: Patients with DS or LGS in Japan are reported to experience substantial seizure and non-seizure burden, and perceived caregiver burden is high. These data underscore the importance of optimized therapies and comprehensive support systems to address both patient and caregiver needs.

papers.title: Clinical features of the postictal state in adults with epilepsy: A cross-sectional survey.
papers.title_zh: 成人癫痫患者发作后状态的临床特征：横断面调查。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Persons with epilepsy may experience many postictal symptoms after a seizure, which can significantly impact quality of life. We aimed to determine the frequency, duration, and severity of postictal symptoms to better characterize the postictal period.
METHODS: Our cross-sectional questionnaire was adapted from a prior pediatric postictal survey. Face and content validity were evaluated by epilepsy experts and patients from the Calgary Epilepsy Program (CEP). The survey was pilot tested and modified, consisting of 14 physical, cognitive, and psychiatric postictal signs and symptoms. Consecutive CEP adults who had agreed to participate in research and experienced a seizure in the prior 2 years were approached. CEP clinical data were used to supplement survey data. Frequency of factors alleviating and exacerbating postictal symptoms were examined. Spearman's rho was used to explore associations between survey and CEP registry data with statistical significance at ≤ 0.05.
RESULTS: Of 351 patients approached, 313 agreed to participate (89%). Fourteen were lost after consent was obtained, and 15 were excluded (incomplete surveys, missing registry data, not having epilepsy). Of the 298 final participants, 54% were female, mean age was 40 years (SD = 15.6), and 95% (282/298) experienced at least one postictal symptom. The three most frequent postictal symptoms were fatigue, sleepiness, or tiredness (84%), confusion or difficulty thinking clearly (75%), and memory problems (69%). For eight of 14 captured postictal symptoms, the most frequently reported symptom duration was <5 min. Mean postictal symptom burden score was correlated with patient reported quality of life and epilepsy-related disability measures. Sleep or rest, medication, and food or drinks were the most common alleviating factors. Lack of rest or sleep, and stress most often exacerbated postictal symptoms.
SIGNIFICANCE: This work contributes toward a better understanding of the postictal period and informs the development of future interventions to minimize the impact of the postictal period in epilepsy.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Neonatal Seizure Detection: A Pragmatic Evaluation of Clinical Performance Tradeoffs in Clinical EEG.
papers.title_zh: 基于人工智能的新生儿癫痫发作检测：对临床脑电图临床性能权衡的实用性评估。
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neurophysiology : official publication of the American Electroencephalographic Society
papers.abstract:
PURPOSE: The aim of this study was to evaluate how three artificial intelligence (AI)-based neonatal seizure detectors (NSDs) perform in a large, clinically acquired data set and their potential to support timely seizure identification.
METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of continuous EEG (cEEG) recordings from 169 neonates born at ≥35 weeks gestation with neonatal encephalopathy. Seizure presence was determined by independent review by two or three pediatric encephalographers, and 2,455 individual seizures were annotated by a single expert as a pragmatic, clinically representative reference standard. Three NSDs were evaluated: a feature-based support vector machine detector (NSD1) and two deep-learning detectors (NSD2 and Persyst-15). Using an any-overlap approach, outcomes included neonate-level seizure identification, seizure-level detection, false detections per day (FD/day), and detection latency.
RESULTS: We analyzed 15,343 hours of cEEG (median 98 hours per neonate); 55 neonates (33%) had seizures. All NSDs identified ≥95% of neonates with seizures. Seizure-level detection varied: NSD2 detected 35% (IQR 17-53%), NSD1 63% (IQR 38-82%), and Persyst-15 60% (IQR 37-80%) of seizures. NSD1 generated significantly more FDs (46 FD/day, IQR 22-82) than NSD2 (3.2 IQR 1.2-9.3) and Persyst-15 (2.8 IQR 1.1-6.2; P < 0.0001). The median time to first true detection was <1 minute for NSD1 and Persyst-15, versus 26 minutes for NSD2.
CONCLUSIONS: AI-based NSDs demonstrated high infant-level sensitivity but different tradeoffs between seizure-level detection and alarm burden. These findings highlight how AI tools may augment clinical EEG workflows and support earlier seizure recognition, while underscoring the need for evaluation under real-world conditions to guide safe and effective implementation.

papers.title: International Survey of Stereo-EEG Practices: A Comparative Analysis of Epilepsy Surgery Centers in Europe and North America.
papers.title_zh: 立体脑电图实践的国际调查：欧洲和北美癫痫手术中心的比较分析。
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neurophysiology : official publication of the American Electroencephalographic Society
papers.abstract:
PURPOSE: Stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) is widely used for presurgical evaluation in epilepsy, yet practice patterns vary substantially across centers, contributing to heterogeneity in the literature. We examined differences in SEEG experience, techniques, and complications across Europe and North America centers.
METHODS: An electronic 39-item REDCap survey was distributed to centers participating in the American Stereo-EEG Consortium and EpiCARE Consortium. The survey assessed center characteristics, electrode planning and implantation, monitoring practices, and complications.
RESULTS: Sixty-six centers responded, including 38 from North America and 28 from Europe. North American centers more frequently used nurse-led ictal and postictal assessments (16/38 vs. 5/28; P = 0.06) and robotic image-guided implantation systems (37/38 vs. 17/28; P < 0.001), with a trend toward higher case volumes. Compared with European centers, North American programs were less likely to have over 15 years of SEEG experience (6/38 vs. 12/28; P = 0.015), fewer dedicated SEEG readers (12/38 vs. 25/28; P < 0.001), and less frequent use of SEEG-guided radiofrequency ablation (13/38 vs. 25/28; P < 0.01). Symptomatic hemorrhage was more frequently reported among North American centers in the unadjusted analysis (9/38 vs. 1/28; p = 0.035); however, the regional difference was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for center SEEG experience and annual case volume.
CONCLUSIONS: Significant differences exist between North American and European SEEG practices. North American centers more commonly use robotic implantation and manage higher volume, whereas European centers demonstrate greater experience and more frequent use of SEEG-guided ablation. These findings support the need for standardized protocols to improve safety and outcomes.

papers.title: Multimodal synthesis of neural correlates of motor imagery after spinal cord injury: a systematic review.
papers.title_zh: 脊髓损伤后运动想象神经关联的多模态合成：系统综述。
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spinal cord injury (SCI) profoundly disrupts motor output while also reshaping central motor systems. Motor imagery (MI) provides a valuable window into retained motor-related neural processes because it enables investigation of covert motor state generation in the absence of overt movement. However, evidence on MI after SCI remains fragmented across neurophysiological and neuroimaging modalities. The objective of this review was to systematically synthesize evidence on the neural correlates of MI after SCI across electroencephalography (EEG), functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), magnetoencephalography (MEG), and intracortical recordings.
METHODS: A systematic search of MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, Embase, and EBSCOhost was conducted from database inception to March 2026. Original studies were included if they involved individuals with SCI, used an explicit MI task, and reported MI-related neural outcomes derived from EEG, fMRI, MEG, or intracortical recordings. Because of substantial heterogeneity in injury profiles, task paradigms, modalities, and neural outcome measures, a narrative synthesis was performed.
RESULTS: Thirty-four studies met the inclusion criteria, including 15 EEG, 10 fMRI, 4 MEG, and 5 intracortical recording studies. Across modalities, MI-related neural activity remained detectable after SCI, with evidence spanning oscillatory responses, regional recruitment, network organization, and fine-grained neural representations. Many studies also described altered recruitment patterns, modified connectivity, atypical task-related modulation, or changes in representational structure. Findings varied according to injury phenotype, chronicity, task design, and analytical framework. The four modalities provided complementary evidence on post-SCI motor imagery across temporal, spatial, network, and neuronal scales.
CONCLUSIONS: Available evidence indicates that MI-related neural activity is generally detectable after SCI, although its organization is often altered. A multimodal perspective is therefore necessary for understanding both the persistence and the reshaping of motor representations after injury. These findings support continued investigation of MI in neurorehabilitation and neurotechnology, while also highlighting the need for approaches that account for post-injury heterogeneity.

papers.title: Different Pipelines, Different EEG Microstate Results: Evidence from Dementia Samples.
papers.title_zh: 不同的处理流程，不同的EEG微状态结果：来自失智症样本的证据。
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) microstate analysis has been proposed as a potential biomarker for neurological disorders, yet the influence of analytic pipeline choices on clinical findings remains unclear. Resting-state EEG from patients with Alzheimer's disease (n = 36), frontotemporal dementia (n = 23), and healthy controls (n = 29) was analyzed using multiple microstate pipelines combining k-means or atomize-agglomerate hierarchical clustering with different temporal-smoothing conditions. Bayesian ANCOVA showed that evidence for group differences varied substantially across pipelines, particularly as a function of temporal smoothing. Rank-correlation analyses further demonstrated reduced agreement between smoothed and unsmoothed pipelines, indicating that smoothing altered the relative ordering of microstate temporal parameters across participants. To assess methodological stability, intra-subject split-half analyses were performed. Microstate topographies showed > 92% shared variance between independent data halves, whereas the reliability of duration, occurrence, and coverage varied across pipelines. Unsmoothed pipelines generally showed equal or greater split-half reliability for selected microstate B measures, and the reproducibility of clinical effect sizes differed by clustering algorithm and diagnostic contrast. These findings demonstrate that temporal smoothing and clustering choices can substantially influence the reliability and clinical interpretation of EEG microstate measures, underscoring the need for explicit pipeline validation in biomarker studies.

papers.title: Electroencephalography Neurophysiology Alterations in Association with Aβ and Tau Pathology Across the Symptomatic Stages of Alzheimer's Disease Continuum: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.title_zh: 在阿尔茨海默病连续性疾病的症状阶段，与Aβ和Tau病理相关的脑电图神经生理学变化：一项横断面研究。
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Amyloid-β (Aβ) and tau deposition drive Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, how these proteinopathies are linked to macroscopic neural activity alterations measured by electroencephalography (EEG) in symptomatic AD remains inadequately characterized. This study aims to investigate the associations between Aβ, tau, EEG neurophysiology, and cognition.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study of 73 MCI and AD participants, who underwent resting-state EEG, Aβ-PET, and tau-PET. EEG source analysis was performed to extract regional spectral power. Linear mixed-effects models were used to examine the associations of regional Aβ (quantified by SUVR), tau (binary classification), with EEG features, controlling for age, sex and education. Ordinary least squares (OLS) regression was applied to investigate the relationships of EEG spectral power and global Aβ burden with cognitive performance.
RESULTS: Elevated Aβ burden was associated with distinct regional spectral alterations. Specifically, higher Aβ SUVR was significantly correlated with increased theta power and decreased beta power in a subset of cortical regions. Tau positivity did not modulate the amyloid-theta association in any region, but attenuated the amyloid-beta association in a small set of parietal regions.
CONCLUSIONS: We identified a localized pattern of Aβ-related neurophysiological dysfunction across the symptomatic stages of AD continuum, characterized by theta increases and beta decreases, supporting a robust association between Aβ burden and cortical neural slowing. The findings highlight the value of source-localized EEG power as a sensitive indicator of Aβ-associated network dysfunction in AD and underscore the potential of source-localized EEG as a complementary, non-invasive biomarker for assessing pathological burden and informing diagnostic strategies in AD.

papers.title: Interictal Electroencephalographic Characteristics of the Human Centromedian Thalamic Nucleus Recorded in Focal Epilepsy.
papers.title_zh: 局灶性癫痫中记录的人类丘脑中腹核间歇期脑电图特征。
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The centromedian (CM) thalamic nucleus is critical in sleep-wake regulation and epileptic networks; yet its electroencephalography (EEG) characteristics remain incompletely understood. CM EEG across vigilance states and interictal epileptic discharges (IEDs) in focal epilepsy were investigated.
METHODS: Interictal stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) recordings from the CM and neighboring ventroposterior (VP) and ventrolateral (VL) nuclei were analyzed with synchronous cortical SEEG and scalp EEG during wakefulness, non-rapid eye movement sleep, rapid eye movement sleep, and spontaneous non-epileptic arousal. Spectral power was quantified across frequency bands. Sleep-related thalamic activities and thalamic IEDs were visually identified.
RESULTS: SEEG data from 33 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy and 3 non-epileptic individuals were analyzed. CM exhibited continuous fast activity during wakefulness and delta/theta-dominant activity during sleep, confirmed by increased gamma-fast ripple power in wakefulness and enhanced delta/theta power in sleep (all p < 0.014). During spontaneous non-epileptic arousal, thalamic EEG changes preceded scalp EEG arousal (median 800 ms; interquartile range: 400-1500 ms). Four sleep-related thalamic EEG activities were reproducibly observed in non-epileptic individuals, supporting a potential physiological nature. Thalamic IEDs occurred in 36.4% of patients with focal epilepsy, invariably involved the CM. Thalamic IEDs were more frequent in extratemporal than temporal lobe epilepsy and were not associated with surgical outcome.
CONCLUSIONS: CM SEEG demonstrates distinct, state-dependent electrophysiological dynamics across the sleep-wake cycle and preferential involvement in interictal epileptic activity compared with VL/VP nuclei.
SIGNIFICANCE: These findings lay the foundation for a thalamic EEG atlas and refine understanding of differential engagement of thalamic nuclei in epileptic networks.

papers.title: Lower frequency ECoG features improve longitudinal stability of speech and hand-grasp detection in a patient with progressive ALS.
papers.title_zh: 低频ECoG特征改善了渐进性肌萎缩侧索硬化症（ALS）患者的语音和握手检测的纵向稳定性。
papers.abstract: Achieving long-term decoding stability is a critical challenge for chronicintracranial brain-computer interfaces (BCIs). High-gamma (HG) activity fromintracranial recordings is the standard signal for BCI control, and lower-frequency featurescan enhance HG decoding performance. This study evaluated the longitudinal stability ofspeech and hand-grasp detection models using individual and joint spectral features, andthe local motor potential (LMP).Approach. Longitudinal data from a single participant implanted with two 64-channelECoG arrays were used to evaluate the long-term stability of logistic regression models forspeech and hand-grasp detection. Models were trained on individual frequency bands andon the LMP, a time-domain low-frequency feature, and evaluated over 21 months forspeech and 13 months for grasp. The best-performing band features were then combinedinto multi-band models and analyzed for their spatial contributions.Main Results. The LMP yielded the most accurate single feature models in both tasks(speech 93.8%, grasp 99.4%) and showed little or no decline. Multi-band modelscombining HG with lower frequency bands were substantially more stable than HG-onlymodels and outperformed the LMP models for speech but not grasp. HG accuracydegraded strongly for both tasks (speech:-4.3 percentage points per 100 days, or pp/100d,grasp:-3.4 pp/100d). HG+beta for speech showed a negligible decline (-0.5 pp/100d,95.6% ±0.06% overall), and for grasp, delta alone showed remarkable stability (+0.5pp/100d), while HG+beta+delta maintained 98.2 ±0.09% overall accuracy with flatperformance (+0.0 pp/100d). The advantage of the multi-band models increased overtime, reaching +20.6 pp for speech and +10.2 pp for grasp in the last 100 days.Significance. Incorporating lower-frequency neural activity yields more stable long-termspeech and grasp detection than HG alone. These findings indicate that lower-frequencyand multi-band features may reduce recalibration requirements for simple BCI tasks, andmay complement the precision control provided by HG activity.

papers.title: Broadband gamma-band EEG changes during magnetophosphene-inducing 20 Hz magnetic field stimulation.
papers.title_zh: 磁光酚诱导20 Hz磁场刺激期间的宽带伽马波段脑电图变化。
papers.abstract: Magnetophosphenes are visual percepts induced by extremely low-frequency magnetic fields (ELF-MF; <300 Hz), yet the EEG expression of suprathreshold magnetophosphene-inducing stimulation remains poorly characterized and is not reliably captured by classical low-frequency markers. We tested whether suprathreshold 20 Hz tAMS is accompanied by broadband high-frequency EEG changes rather than focal oscillatory effects. EEG was recorded in N=13 healthy volunteers during 20 Hz sinusoidal magnetic-field exposure delivered using transcranial alternating magnetic stimulation (tAMS) in a global-head configuration. Three conditions were analyzed: no exposure (0 mT), subthreshold (5 mT), and suprathreshold (50 mT). Gamma-band EEG power (30-80 Hz) was quantified using complementary spectral approaches, including aperiodic-adjusted gamma power. Perception reports sharply dissociated the three conditions, with frequent perception at 50 mT only. Suprathreshold stimulation was associated with spatially distributed increases in gamma-band EEG power over frontal and occipito-parietal electrodes. The differences remained partly detectable in complementary analyses using two local aperiodic-adjustment methods and did not exhibit a consistent narrowband peak, a pattern consistent with broadband high-frequency changes. No focal power change over primary occipital electrodes remained significant after Bonferroni correction. These findings identify a spatially distributed broadband high-frequency scalp EEG effect associated with the suprathreshold 50 mT condition, with the main spatial pattern strongly preserved after ICA-based removal of components classified as ocular or muscular. The effect therefore characterizes the coupled suprathreshold stimulation-perception condition; its perception specificity and physiological source remain unresolved.

papers.title: Automated intracranial spike analysis across sleep-wake states localizes the seizure onset zone in drug-resistant epilepsy.
papers.title_zh: 跨睡眠-觉醒状态的自动颅内尖峰分析确定了耐药性癫痫的癫痫发作区。
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) are an established biomarker of epilepsy, but their utility for seizure-onset zone (SOZ) localization has been limited by reliance on short recording samples, research-grade detectors, and a primary focus on spike frequency. We assessed multi-day intracranial IED activity across sleep-wake states and its ability to localize the SOZ in adults and children.
METHODS: We analyzed simultaneous scalp and intracranial EEG data from 17 patients in the EPILEPSIAE database (predominantly adult) and 10 pediatric patients at the Alberta Children's Hospital (ACH), with 48 to 72 h of data per patient. FDA-cleared clinical software (Persyst P15a) performed automated sleep staging and IED detection. We introduced a novel IED activity metric reflecting IED amplitude and the relative consistency of channel participation across detected events and used logistic regression with leave-one-patient-out cross-validation to predict SOZ channels for each sleep-wake state.
RESULTS: IED activity was significantly higher in SOZ than in non-SOZ channels across every sleep-wake state in both cohorts. N2 sleep yielded the highest AUROC for SOZ localization (0.69 EPILEPSIAE; 0.77 ACH), but differences across states were not statistically significant. The presence of clinical seizures during the recording did not significantly affect localization performance.
CONCLUSIONS: Automated intracranial IED analysis localizes the SOZ in adults and children, with only modest variation across sleep-wake states.
SIGNIFICANCE: Amplitude-aware IED analysis using clinically deployed software is a practical adjunct to presurgical SOZ localization. The modest effect of sleep-wake states suggests that clinical value can be obtained without state-specific analysis. This approach may strengthen presurgical evaluation in adult and pediatric drug-resistant epilepsy.

papers.title: Flexible recording electrodes preliminarily reveal the brain-spinal circuit mechanism of spinal cord stimulation in the treatment of motor impairment in the mouse model of Parkinson's disease.
papers.title_zh: 柔性记录电极初步揭示了脊髓电刺激在帕金森病小鼠模型运动障碍治疗中的脑-脊髓环路机制。
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by motor impairment, including gait disorders and postural instability, while the efficacy of pharmacological therapy and deep brain stimulation remains limited. In recent years, the potential of spinal cord electrical stimulation (SCS) has attracted significant attention in the treatment of movement disorders, but its underlying mechanism remains unclear. Owing to their excellent biocompatibility and high spatiotemporal resolution, flexible recording electrodes are regarded as important tools for decoding the motor circuits. In the present study, flexible recording electrodes were used to chronically record brain signals in the PD mouse model and to explore the regulatory mechanism of SCS in the brain-spinal cord motor circuit. The results demonstrate that SCS effectively ameliorates motor impairment in the PD mouse model. Moreover, the spectral power of the theta-band (4-10 Hz) recorded in the primary motor (M1) cortex of PD mice significantly increased after SCS. Collectively, this study comprehensively evaluated the therapeutic effects of SCS in a PD mouse model and identified cortical theta-band activity as a potential electrophysiological marker, which may provide evidence for the closed-loop application of SCS in clinical practice.

papers.title: Electroconvulsive therapy for the treatment of depression: from convulsive treatment to precision neuromodulation.
papers.title_zh: 电惊厥疗法治疗抑郁症：从惊厥治疗到精准神经调节。
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: ECT remains one of the most effective treatments for severe depression, including psychotic and treatment-resistant presentations and high-acuity cases requiring rapid response. This review examines ECT as a parameter-sensitive neuromodulation procedure rather than a fixed convulsive treatment.
AREAS COVERED: We review historical development, clinical efficacy, safety, relapse prevention, and mechanistic models involving seizure induction, electric-field effects, inhibitory plasticity, neurochemical and neuroendocrine signaling, network change, and postictal brain states. The literature was identified through searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar from database inception to June 2026, supplemented by reference-list screening, with evidence evaluated according to study design, clinical relevance, and technological maturity. Established components of contemporary ECT practice are distinguished from near-term optimization strategies and experimental technologies.
EXPERT OPINION: Precision ECT should be regarded as an emerging framework rather than an established standard of care. Patient-specific electric-field modeling, biomarker-guided dosing, amplitude optimization, and adaptive stimulation are promising strategies for improving the therapeutic index, but require prospective validation against optimized standard ECT using clinical, cognitive, and patient-reported outcomes.

papers.title: Recent applications of neural interfaces in musculoskeletal disorders: from rehabilitation to regeneration.
papers.title_zh: 神经接口在肌肉骨骼疾病中的最新应用：从康复到再生。
papers.abstract: Musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) represent a primary cause of global long-term disability, stemming from musculoskeletal tissue damage or impaired neural motor and homeostatic regulation. The musculoskeletal system participates in a bidirectional neuro-musculoskeletal-immune network, explaining why conventional tissue repair and mechanical rehabilitation often fail to fully restore tissue and motor function. Neural interface (NI)-based bioelectronic medicine provides a precise, translational strategy to reconstruct disrupted neural commands, remodel abnormal sensory pathways, and regulate local inflammation and metabolism for MSD recovery. This review comprehensively summarizes recent NI applications in diverse MSDs, including structural injuries and degenerative diseases, as well as functional deficits induced by spinal cord injury, stroke and peripheral nerve damage. We highlight the clinical transition from open-loop stimulation and passive assistive devices to closed-loop adaptive neuromodulation systems for motor control, sensory restoration and pain relief, alongside emerging bioelectronic regenerative strategies. We further discuss advanced NI material and system designs, covering multimodal sensing, low-latency neuromorphic computing and energy-autonomous modules. Key translational barriers and a roadmap for next-generation regenerative MSD therapies are finally outlined.

papers.title: Closed-loop transcranial electrical brain stimulation with fMRI: A proof-of-concept randomized trial of real-time fMRI-guided tACS optimization.
papers.title_zh: 结合fMRI的闭环经颅电刺激：一项实时fMRI引导的tACS优化概念验证随机试验。
papers.abstract: Closed-loop transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) combined with real-time functional MRI (tACS-fMRI) enables adaptive optimization of noninvasive brain stimulation based on ongoing neural dynamics. We implemented one of the first randomized, double-arm, closed-loop tACS-fMRI protocols to iteratively adjust stimulation frequency and phase alignment between the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (F4) and right inferior parietal cortex (P4) to modulate frontoparietal functional connectivity (FFC) during a 2-back working memory task. Twenty healthy adults were randomized to an up-regulation group (n = 10), receiving parameters optimized to maintain or enhance FFC, or a down-regulation group (n = 10), receiving parameters optimized to reduce FFC using a simplex-based adaptive algorithm across two training runs. Individualized optimized parameters were applied during a subsequent test run, with resting-state fMRI acquired before and after stimulation. During the test phase, connectivity trajectories diverged across groups: FFC was preserved in the up-regulation group but declined in the down-regulation group (signed-rank p = 0.019), with a significant between-group difference confirmed by permutation testing (20,000 iterations; p = 0.043). Behavioral effects were primarily observed in the accuracy learning dynamics. Although overall mean performance was comparable, the up-regulation group demonstrated a more positive accuracy trajectory, greater within-test accuracy gain (p = 0.036), and steeper trial-wise improvement (p = 0.035). Reaction time decreased across runs in both groups, consistent with practice effects, with no significant group differences in gain; however, the test-run RT slope showed a trend toward a steeper reduction in reaction time in the up-regulation group relative to the down-regulation group (p = 0.065). Resting-state analyses revealed significant time-by-group interaction clusters in seed-based connectivity (voxel-wise p < 0.001; cluster-level FDR p < 0.05), with connectivity increases observed in the up-regulation group relative to the down-regulation group, indicating persistent network modulation following stimulation. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of closed-loop tACS-fMRI for individualized network-targeted neuromodulation and suggest that real-time connectivity optimization selectively stabilizes task-relevant connectivity and enhances accuracy learning while producing sustained effects on intrinsic brain networks.

papers.title: Near-Infrared Neuromodulation: Principles, Nanotechnology-Enabled Platforms, and Emerging Biomedical Frontiers.
papers.title_zh: 近红外神经调节：原理，纳米技术支持的平台和新兴的生物医学前沿。
papers.abstract: Optogenetics enables highly specific regulation of neuronal activity with exceptional spatiotemporal precision, providing powerful tools for neural circuit interrogation and the treatment of neurological disorders. However, the limited tissue penetration of visible light restricts its application to deep neural tissues. Near-infrared (NIR) neuromodulation has emerged as a promising alternative by leveraging the superior tissue penetration and minimal invasiveness of NIR light. Recent advances in NIR-responsive nanomaterials, optical engineering, and neurotechnology have rapidly transformed the field from nonspecific photobiomodulation to cell-specific nanotransducer-mediated neuromodulation and integrated neuromodulation systems. In this review, we summarize the optical principles governing NIR propagation in biological tissues and the mechanisms underlying NIR-mediated neural stimulation. We then discuss recent advances in representative NIR nanotransducers, including photothermal, optoelectric, photoacoustic, and NIR-to-visible upconversion platforms together with integrated neuromodulation systems that combine NIR stimulation with multimodal neural recording and closed-loop feedback. We further highlight emerging applications in the central nervous system, optic nerve, and peripheral nerve disorders. Finally, we discuss the key challenges toward clinical translation, including improving tissue penetration, cell specificity, biosafety, and translation, developing intelligent multidisciplinary neuromodulation platforms, and integrating artificial intelligence with closed-loop neural interfaces to achieve adaptive, precise, and personalized neuromodulation.

papers.title: Molecular origami in neuroscience: noncanonical DNA structures and functional nucleic acids in neural regulation and disease.
papers.title_zh: 神经科学中的分子折纸：神经调节和疾病中的非规范DNA结构和功能核酸。
papers.abstract: Gliomas are increasingly recognized as network diseases in which aberrant interactions between tumor cells, neurons, and immune populations drive hyperexcitability, seizures, cognitive dysfunction, and disease progression. Simultaneously, advances in structural biology and nucleic acid engineering have revealed DNA to be a dynamic molecular architecture capable of sensing, regulating, and modulating cellular states. In this review, we examine how noncanonical DNA structures and functional nucleic acids including Z-DNA, G-quadruplexes, cruciform structures, aptamers, and DNA origami systems, shape neural regulation and glioma associated circuit pathology. We discuss how activity dependent DNA conformational transitions influence transcriptional programs controlling neurotransmission, ion channel expression, synaptic signaling, metabolism, and inflammatory pathways in glioma cells and peritumoral neural networks. Z-DNA formation appears linked to rapid transcriptional activation and enhancer dynamics, whereas G-quadruplex rich regulatory regions modulate genes associated with excitatory signaling, cellular proliferation, and tumor progression. Cruciform DNA structures additionally interface with genome stability and DNA repair, creating mechanistic entry points for therapeutic intervention. Beyond endogenous DNA architectures, we highlight the emergence of aptamer based diagnostics and therapeutics capable of detecting neurotransmitters, cytokines, and metabolites associated with glioma induced network dysfunction. DNA origami platforms further enable programmable multivalent delivery systems for targeted transport of small molecules, oligonucleotides, CRISPR machinery, and ion-channel modulators across the neurovascular unit and tumor microenvironment. We also explore closed-loop neuromodulatory strategies in which electrophysiological signatures guide state dependent therapeutic actuation through nucleic acid based sensing and delivery systems. Finally, we discuss key translational considerations, including blood brain barrier delivery, nuclease stability, immunogenicity, biodistribution, manufacturing reproducibility, and integration with existing neuro-oncology and anti-seizure therapies. By bridging molecular origami, electrophysiology, and neurotechnology, this review proposes a framework for precision neuromedicine in glioma and broader neurological disease, where programmable nucleic acid architectures are coupled to the dynamic circuit states that drive pathology.

papers.title: Potential Applications of Brain-Computer Interface Technology in the Rehabilitation of Patients with Anxiety Disorders: A Narrative Review.
papers.title_zh: 脑机接口技术在焦虑症患者康复中的潜在应用：叙事综述。
papers.abstract: Anxiety disorders are among the most prevalent mental disorders worldwide and can cause persistent impairment in emotional regulation, cognition, and social functioning. Pharmacotherapy, psychotherapy, exercise, and non-invasive brain stimulation are widely used, yet their effectiveness may be constrained by dependence liability, interindividual variability, treatment engagement, incomplete response, and limited objective measures of treatment processes. Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) acquire, decode, and feed back neural signals-most commonly electroencephalography (EEG), functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), or real-time functional magnetic resonance imaging (rt-fMRI)-thereby converting anxiety-related brain activity into targets that can be monitored, trained, or used to trigger intervention. This narrative review examines the mechanistic rationale for BCI-assisted anxiety rehabilitation, technological approaches across levels of invasiveness, and integration with pharmacological, psychological, and exercise-based care. Current evidence indicates that EEG has been used for both anxiety-state recognition and neurofeedback; rt-fMRI enables targeted modulation of deep emotion-related networks and functional connectivity; and fNIRS offers promise for portable prefrontal monitoring and as an input signal for closed-loop systems. Invasive closed-loop systems can directly record from and stimulate local or deep circuits, but anxiety-related evidence is derived mainly from animal studies, patients undergoing intracranial monitoring, and neurological populations with comorbid anxiety, and therefore demonstrates technical feasibility rather than efficacy in primary anxiety disorders. Overall, BCIs are better positioned as potential adjuncts to established care than as replacements. The field remains limited by small, single-center studies, inadequate follow-up, heterogeneous acquisition and training protocols, and unresolved governance of neural data. Because this is a narrative review without a formal risk-of-bias assessment or meta-analysis, its conclusions should be regarded as exploratory. Multicenter randomized controlled trials, harmonized technical and reporting standards, cross-device external validation, and risk-proportionate ethical and regulatory frameworks are needed to determine whether BCIs can be translated from proof of concept into safe, effective, and implementable tools for anxiety rehabilitation.

papers.title: Closed-Loop Vagus Nerve Stimulation for Poststroke Motor Recovery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Movement-Synchronized Neuromodulation.
papers.title_zh: 用于中风后运动恢复的闭环迷走神经刺激：运动同步神经调节的系统综述和荟萃分析。
papers.journal: Neuromodulation : journal of the International Neuromodulation Society
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Closed-loop or movement-synchronized vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) has emerged as a promising neuromodulatory strategy to enhance activity-dependent neuroplasticity after stroke. Unlike conventional open-loop stimulation, closed-loop VNS is temporally coupled with motor execution, potentially improving the specificity and efficacy of motor recovery. However, clinical evidence remains fragmented, and no prior meta-analysis has specifically evaluated this approach. This study aimed to systematically assess the effectiveness and safety of closed-loop VNS for upper-limb motor recovery after stroke.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Electronic data bases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science) were searched from inception to March 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) investigating movement-synchronized VNS in adult patients with a clinical diagnosis of stroke presenting with upper limb motor impairment were included. Primary outcomes were changes in Fugl-Meyer Assessment of Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) and Wolf Motor Function Test (WMFT). Data were pooled using a random-effects model, and effect sizes were expressed as mean difference (MD) or standardized mean difference (SMD) with 95% CI. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB2, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation.
RESULTS: Six RCTs comprising 215 participants were included in the quantitative synthesis, with an additional cohort study included qualitatively. Closed-loop VNS demonstrated a significant improvement in FMA-UE scores compared with controls (MD = 2.33, 95% CI 0.95-3.70, p = 0.0009), although with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 89%). WMFT outcomes from four RCTs (n ≈ 177) also favored closed-loop VNS (SMD = 0.62, 95% CI 0.25-0.98, p = 0.0009) with low heterogeneity (I2 = 18%). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the stability of the findings, whereas meta-regression showed no significant effect of age. The pooled adverse-event analysis of two implanted VNS trials showed no statistically significant between-group difference, although estimates were highly imprecise. Overall certainty of evidence was moderate.
CONCLUSION: Closed-loop or movement-synchronized VNS may provide clinically meaningful improvements in upper-limb motor function after stroke; however, the available safety evidence is limited and imprecise, particularly for implanted VNS, and cannot be generalized to noninvasive transcutaneous auricular VNS.
